newsitem.title: PANAMA: Colombian inmates sew mouths in protest in Panama.
newsitem.headline: Colombian inmates sew mouths in protest in Panama.

text.p: Thirty hunger striking Colombian inmates at a Panamanian prison have sewn their mouths shut in protest against alleged human rights violations, Interior Minister Raul Montenegro said Thursday.
Thirty-four prisoners, including 30 Colombians, have demanded better living conditions, including the right to receive family visits, make international telephone calls and eat better food.
"They (the prisoners) are not there to be given a prize for good work but to pay through imprisonment for their crimes," Montenegro told local RPC television network.
RPC said the 30 Colombians were in prison for drug trafficking and added that they had sewed their mouth shut with string and wire.
Local newspaper La Prensa reported that the prisoners had been on hunger strike since Monday.
European Union representatives who visited La Joya and other prisons in Panama Thursday lambasted the Panamanian authorities for the treatment of inmates.

"Many of the inmates are in spaces which are not equipped even for the minimal health requirements and the minimum human rights which they should have," European Union representative Alain Blanc said.
La Joya prison houses over 1,200 inmates in Panama City.
